title: Adaptive regional thresholding and latency rollups for token-level SLIs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We currently have token-level latency SLI instrumentation scoped per global endpoint but lack compact regional rollups and adaptive thresholds tied to deployment topology (capacity tier, model variant, and region). This makes automated regional failover and circuit-breaker decisioning noisy during transient spikes.

Goal: Add a set of rollup metrics and dashboards that enable: (1) precise token-level SLIs per region/model_variant/route, (2) adaptive thresholding logic inputs for regional circuit breakers and load-shedding policies, and (3) compact visuals for on-call and SRE runbooks to execute failover and throttling actions.

Scope:
- Instrument new metrics in serving runtime (C++) and ingress proxy (Go) to emit pre-aggregated rollups at 10s and 1m intervals for p50/p90/p95/p99 token latency, tail-count, and effective shed_rate.
- Tagging dimensions: region, availability_zone (optional), capacity_tier (hosted/dedicated/private), model_family, model_variant, route, and shard_id.
- Circuit-breaker telemetry: circuit_state{open|closed|half_open} with reason tag, open_count, close_count, attempts_since_open, and shed_decisions_count.
- Add derived metrics: rolling_inflight_batches, kv_cache_hit_rate_by_region, prefix_cache_latency_ms, and regional_error_budget_burn_rate.
- Dashboards: regional rollup heatmap, model-variant latency trend, circuit-breaker activity timeline, failover sequence diagram with timestamps, and a compact on-call playbook panel showing current SLO burn and recommended action.
- Alerts: SLO burn-rate alerting per-region with adaptive thresholds (see acceptance criteria).

Acceptance criteria:
1) New rollup metrics emit from runtime and are ingested by metrics pipeline (prometheus -> cortex) with correct tags and cardinality limits documented.
2) Dashboards created in Grafana with panels for p95/p99 by region and model_variant, and a heatmap for regional tail latency and shed_rate.
3) Circuit breaker metrics surface in dashboard and feed the orchestration service for automated failover decisions.
4) SRE-runbook updated and validated in an on-call tabletop exercise (link in comments).
5) No more than 20% additional cardinality to metric store for serving-related metrics (implement sampling/rollup if needed).

Implementation notes:
- Use a two-tier rollup strategy: emit fine-grained per-shard metrics internally (high cardinality) but only forward aggregated rollups (region+model_variant+route) to global metrics backend.
- For adaptive thresholds, compute short-window (1m) p99 and long-window (1h) baseline; threshold = max(fixed_floor_ms, baseline * multiplier) where multiplier is 1.5 for hosted and 2.0 for dedicated during warmup.
- Provide Prometheus recording rules for rollup metrics to reduce query cost.
- Add feature flag to gate metric emission by customer tier to control cost during rollout.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch: add metric emission hooks and local unit tests (runtime).
2) Canary in one non-prod region for one model_family and route; validate rollups and dashboard panels.
3) Incrementally enable for 25% of traffic in a secondary region, validate on-call playbook.
4) Global enable with rate-limited cardinality caps and sampling fallbacks.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Cardinality explosion if we emit per-shard rollups to global backend; mitigated by server-side aggregation and sampling.
- Slight CPU overhead in runtime to compute quantiles: use t-digest library with bounded memory and export only rollups.
- Potential alert noise during rollout: use staged alerting and mute until canary stable.

Documentation and links: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Adaptive+Regional+Thresholds (draft); Design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED; PR (infra): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3456
